newsitem.title: ITALY: Panic, CO2 killed six on tanker - Italian shipyard.
newsitem.headline: Panic, CO2 killed six on tanker - Italian shipyard.

text.p: Six workers killed in a fire during a tanker's sea trials off Genoa on Wednesday were suffocated by fire extinguishers switched on in panic, state shipyard Fincantieri said on Friday.
The victims died of asphyxia after the carbon dioxide extinguisher system of the methane gas tanker SNAM Portovenere, was turned on during a blaze in the engine room.
Three other workers were injured. The tanker was empty.

The new vessel, the largest of its type constructed in Italy, had 188 people on board, many of them technicians and engineers carrying out tests. The ship was due to be delivered to SNAM, a unit of state energy group ENI.

Fincantieri said the fire broke out at 0400 GMT in the engine room. Crew managed to contain it with portable fire extinguishers but apparently someone activated the onboard carbon dioxide or CO2 fire extinguisher system.
Fincantieri said this system does not come on automatically but can only be activated manually. "None of the officers on board gave this order," the shipbuilder's statement said.
"Unfortunately the activation of the CO2 system, which not ordered by an officer, caught the people present in the engine room by surprise causing their suffocation," it said.

Fincantieri engineer and chief designer of the new tanker Roberto Gonan was quoted in Friday's Corriere della Sera as saying that the CO2 system was "lethal" and was meant to be used only in extreme circumstances.
"It should not have been set off. Whoever did so must have been panicking and made an error of judgement," Gonan said. "Only 10 people on board the ship knew how to make the system work," he added.

The tanker has been towed to Genoa. The cause of the blaze is not yet known and magistrates are still carrying out an investigation into the accident. An autopsy on the victims is due to be held today.
